audit.why: Even-to-hard poke lane: Mel owns 1-2 and first item, Viktor owns 3-6 and 2+ items via shielded trades and evolved CC.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[] and whys[] use pre-rework ability names (Death Ray, Chaos Storm) and claim his E out-ranges Mel's Q (525 vs 950 — false) and that his R silences (it does not).
audit.why: Kit file: E = Hextech Ray 525 range, R = Arcane Storm — damage storm that follows/redirects and interrupts channels, no silence.
audit.corrected: Names fixed to Hextech Ray / Arcane Storm; range and silence claims rewritten from the kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Missing: Viktor's Arcane Storm (R) is a channel Mel's Solar Snare (E) root can cancel; his combo opens on the Siphon Power auto-reset tell. Rebuttal reflects his Q and Hextech Ray (projectiles) but not Gravity Field or the storm (zones).
audit.why: Kit flags: viktor R channel:interruptible, Q autoReset; W and R are zones, E projectile. Missing-interactions file lists both.
audit.corrected: Folded into spikes[1], dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.why: Short-trade-around-his-shield pattern is right; sharpened dosFull[1].d to key on Q shield cooldown (9-5s).
Kit gives Gravity Field 17/16/15/14/13, Hextech Ray 12-8, Mel W 38-26, R 120/100/80.

audit.whatIsWrong: Solar Snare cancelling Arcane Storm's channel was never stated.

edits.before: Late Mel is a counter-artillery battery: reflect their poke, snare their dive, and execute the chipped.
edits.after: Evolved Gravity Field into Arcane Storm chains CC through the reflect — punish from range, never duel.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. It governs your forward steps. - W Rebuttal spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Gravity Field: 17s at rank 1, 13s max — the stun zone owns every all-in; walk out when it drops or fight in that window. - Hextech Ray cycles every 12-8s between shield gaps. - W Rebuttal (38s early) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold R (120s) for the fight that decides.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: His Q shield is on a 9-5s cooldown — time your volleys for the gap after it breaks and the chip actually sticks.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Gravity Field and Arcane Storm are zones, not projectiles — Rebuttal reflects his Q and Hextech Ray, nothing else he casts.

edits.before: Level 3 flips to Viktor because Death Ray out-ranges your Q and pushes you off the wave.
edits.after: Level 3 flips to Viktor as Hextech Ray plus his Q shield lets him shove and win long trades.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay Viktor's since Siphon Power shields your return poke and his laser controls the trade.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay Viktor's since Siphon Power shields your return poke and Hextech Ray clears waves.

edits.before: Level 6 is Viktor's as Chaos Storm silences you out of your kit and Gravity Field sets up his pick.
edits.after: Level 6 is Viktor's as Arcane Storm chases you down and Gravity Field's stun sets up the full pick.

edits.before: At 2+ items Viktor wins again as evolved Gravity Field into Chaos Storm chains CC through your reflect and out-DPSes you.
edits.after: At 2+ items Viktor wins again as evolved Gravity Field into Arcane Storm chains CC through your reflect and out-DPSes you.

edits.before: Once Viktor has Death Ray (E) he out-ranges and out-clears you: the laser pokes you off the wave and his Siphon Power (Q) shield eats your Radiant Volley (Q) return. Don't stand in the caster minions and don't walk into Gravity Field (W) or you eat a free E.
edits.after: Once Viktor has Hextech Ray (E) he out-clears you: the laser sweeps the wave and his Siphon Power (Q) shield eats your Radiant Volley (Q) return. Don't stand in the caster minions and don't walk into Gravity Field (W) or you eat a free E on top of the stun.

edits.before: Chaos Storm (R) silences and follows you, shutting off your Solar Snare (E) and Rebuttal (W) at the worst moment; combined with W-stun he has a full pick combo. Save your Flash for the storm and never fight while silenced.
edits.after: Arcane Storm (R) follows you and combined with the Gravity Field stun he has a full pick combo. The storm is itself a channel — your Solar Snare (E) root cancels it outright, so keep the root in pocket and never fight inside the field.

edits.before: Your first-item timing is the one window you own: Mel's item spike lands before Viktor evolves his augments, so W can reflect his Death Ray and E can punish him if he steps up to clear. Force short trades here and roam while he's still a farming Viktor.
edits.after: Your first-item timing is the one window you own: Mel's item spike lands before Viktor evolves his augments, so W can reflect his Hextech Ray and E can punish him if he steps up to clear. Force short trades here and roam while he's still a farming Viktor.

edits.before: Two items in, evolved Viktor overwhelms you: augmented Gravity Field into Chaos Storm chains CC through your reflect and his poke out-DPSes your combo. Only fight when W is up to eat his E, and let your team engage while you punish from max range.
edits.after: Two items in, evolved Viktor overwhelms you: augmented Gravity Field into Arcane Storm chains CC through your reflect and his poke out-DPSes your combo. Only fight when W is up to eat his E, and let your team engage while you punish from max range.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are yours before Death Ray comes online: your Radiant Volley (Q) and passive autos out-trade his weak early poke, and he's forced to walk up for CS with no shield uptime. Bully him now to slow his early Hex Core purchases.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours before Hextech Ray comes online: your Radiant Volley (Q) and passive autos out-trade his weak early poke, and he's forced to walk up for CS with little shield uptime. Bully him now and slow his Hex Fragment farm.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 belong to Viktor. Death Ray (E) out-ranges your Q and shoves you off the wave, Siphon Power (Q) shields your poke, and at 6 Chaos Storm (R) silences you out of your entire kit while Gravity Field (W) sets up the pick. Farm from max range and refuse to trade into his laser.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 belong to Viktor. Hextech Ray (E) sweeps the wave every 12-8s, Siphon Power (Q) shields your return poke, and at 6 Arcane Storm (R) chases you down while Gravity Field (W) sets up the pick. Farm from your 950-range Q and refuse extended trades into his laser.

edits.before: Your first mage item is the single window where you're ahead, before his augment evolutions land; abuse it with reflected Death Rays and short E trades. Once he's two items and evolved, his chained W-into-R CC and relentless poke reclaim control, so fight only with W ready and let your frontline absorb the storm.
edits.after: Your first mage item is the single window where you're ahead, before his augment evolutions land; abuse it with reflected Hextech Rays and short E trades. Once he's two items and evolved, his chained W-into-R CC and relentless poke reclaim control, so fight only with W ready and let your frontline absorb the storm.
